title: bug: `ValidArgsFunction` receives partial input when argument contains colons in Bash

comments.body:
I assume this might be related to COMP_WORDBREAKS which contains `:` by default.
https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bash-Variables.html#index-COMP_005fWORDBREAKS

I had some problems in the original version when this was being added, https://github.com/spf13/cobra/pull/1146#issuecomment-652642489, for outputting such values but I never noticed such issues and in fact on my system your reproducer does not show the issue, I get `args: [], toComplete: "local:/"`

```
$ echo $COMP_WORDBREAKS 
"'><=;|&(:
```

Tested on `bash-5.3.0-2.fc43.x86_64`

What is in the debug bash log completion log, i.e. set the log with `export BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE=repro.debug` then press tab again

This shows it working fine in my system:
```
========= starting completion logic ==========
cur is local:/, words[*] is ./repro ls local:/, #words[@] is 3, cword is 2
Truncated words[*]: ./repro ls local:/,
lastParam local:/, lastChar /
Calling ./repro __complete ls local:/
The completion directive is: 4
The completions are: local:/tmp/file1
local:/tmp/file2

Activating no file completion
__repro_handle_completion_types: COMP_TYPE is 9
```

I have written a ton of code which uses colon or equal signs in completion and have never seen user reports on podman that shell completion does not work properly, i.e. check completeKeyValues() here
https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/cmd/podman/common/completion.go

So I assume this is likely related to some environmental factor and not a general problem.
